title: core `temporalStorageForm`: the `date` arm leaves a year outside 1000..9999 unpadded — over REST the epoch-ms number for 0999-06-15 counts `$gt` 0 / `$lt` 7 on InMemoryDriver and SQLite (correct 6 / 0); its ISO string counts 6 / 0
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-storage-form.ts`, `canonicalCalendarDay`, the `Date`/number arm of the `date` rule. `y` comes from `getUTCFullYear()` and is spelled `${y}-${m}-${d}`. The month and day are padded to width 2; the year is never padded to width 4, and a negative or 5-digit year has no fixed-width form.

Finding class **(a)**. `reach:` was measured at the public REST door on `main` `615c468746` (below).

The `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`) filed this from its #20203 dev's report (`os-dev-report` 5855694754, `out_of_scope_findings[1]` and `open_questions[0]`), under seat ruling 5855727555 (A: file separately). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

- Before PR #20224 (#20203), only an in-process `Date` reached this arm: a `Date` is not JSON.
- Since `615c468746`, a finite epoch-ms number on a `date` field takes the same conversion, so the unpadded spelling is reachable over REST.
- A direct rule call at `615c468746` gives:
  - `0999-06-15`: the number and the `Date` both spell `"999-06-15"`, but the ISO string `"0999-06-15T00:00:00.000Z"` spells `"0999-06-15"`;
  - `10000-01-01`: the number spells `"10000-01-01"`;
  - year −1: the number spells `"-1-01-01"`.

Measured on `main` `615c468746` through `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` (a real `RestServer`, a JSON round-tripped body, `TZ=America/New_York`). The drivers are a real `InMemoryDriver`, a real `SqlDriver` on better-sqlite3, and a live PostgreSQL 16. The fixture is seven rows of a `date` field `placed_on`: six 2026 days, plus `"0999-06-15"` written through the REST create door (201 on all three drivers, read back verbatim).

| comparand | op | memory | SQLite | PostgreSQL | correct |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| number for 0999-06-15 (`-30627504000000`) | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | **0 / 7 / 0** | **0 / 7 / 0** | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 |
| ISO `"0999-06-15T00:00:00.000Z"` | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 |
| bare day `"0999-06-15"` | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 | 6 / 0 / 1 |
| number for 10000-01-01 (`253402300800000`) | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | **6 / 1** / 0 | **6 / 1** / 0 | 0 / 7 / 0 | 0 / 7 / 0 |
| number for −1-01-01 (`-62198755200000`) | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | 7 / 0 / 0 | 7 / 0 / 0 | **500 / 500 / 500** | 7 / 0 / 0 |
| control, number for 2026-02-01T10:00Z | `$gt` / `$lt` / `$eq` | 1 / 4 / 2 | 1 / 4 / 2 | 1 / 4 / 2 | 1 / 4 / 2 |

- **The number and the ISO string for the same day give opposite answers** on InMemoryDriver and SQLite: `"999-06-15"` sorts above every padded `YYYY-MM-DD` as text (`'9' > '0'`), and `"10000-01-01"` sorts below `"2026-…"`. PostgreSQL reads them through its native `DATE` parser and answers correctly.
- The year −1 counts on memory and SQLite are right only by accident: a leading `-` sorts below every digit.
- PostgreSQL answers HTTP 500 `{"error":"Internal server error","code":"DATABASE_ERROR"}` for year −1. The driver log reads: `[sql-driver] DATABASE_ERROR — the backend refused a read on 'year_probe_object' (22009) … where "placed_on" > $1 - time zone displacement out of range: "-62198755200000"`. That value is the raw number, not the rule's `"-1-01-01"`. Which layer passes the raw number to PostgreSQL is not established.
- The #20224 review (5855881108, item 8) measured the same cells at the PR head, and found four extreme-year cells worse than before that PR. Before it, a raw number never met the day text.
- **No measured writer** stores or queries days outside 1000..9999. The reach is the public query door, not an observed caller.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

A decision, then one edit in the one rule (`temporalStorageForm`, `@objectstack/core`). ⛔ Not a copy in a driver.
- Years 0..999: pad to 4 digits (`0999-06-15`), which is the spelling the ISO-string and bare-day arms already produce.
- Years past 9999 and below 0 have no `YYYY-MM-DD` spelling. Decide one reading: refuse at the temporal-comparand door (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400) as outside the `date` range, or define an ordered form. This moves `Date` cells, deliberately.
- Pin on memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL through the engine and REST, with the number, the `Date` and the ISO string for the same day, plus the 2026 control.
- Related: `driver-mongodb`'s own `storageDateValue` copy (an acceptance note in PR #20202 and PR #20224, carrier none).

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (a defect with a named landing site); finding class (a), measured on `main`.
- **Acting reader**: this lane's seat (`domain:engine`, the owner of `packages/core` and the SQL / memory drivers).
- **Dedupe**, MCP semantic issue search in this repo, `closed` included:
  - `date field year below 1000 unpadded calendar day spelling getUTCFullYear YYYY-MM-DD` → 0 hits;
  - `toDateOnly year padding extended year 10000 negative year date comparand text order` → 0;
  - `date year spelling padding` → 0;
  - `temporalStorageForm date arm Date before year 1000` → 0;
  - `date calendar day four digit year ISO extended year` → 0;
  - `date out of range year DateTimeParseError 22008 date field` → 1 hit, #3942 (MySQL `TIMESTAMP` range, closed), which is not this.
  - Control query: `epoch millisecond number against a date field` → #20203, the parent, closed.

Dedupe words: `date arm year not padded to four digits` · `calendar day spelling year outside 1000 9999` · `epoch ms number year 999 date field text order`
